```{python}
#| output: false
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
from pathlib import Path
from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_point, geom_line, geom_col, geom_abline, geom_jitter,
    labs, theme_minimal, coord_flip, scale_color_manual,
)
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import HTML, display
from sportsdataverse.pwhl import pwhl_xg_proxy as mx

ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "pwhl" / "pbp" / "parquet").is_dir():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
PBP_DIR = ROOT / "pwhl" / "pbp" / "parquet"
SEASONS = sorted(int(p.stem.split("_")[-1]) for p in PBP_DIR.glob("play_by_play_*.parquet"))
pbp = {y: pl.read_parquet(PBP_DIR / f"play_by_play_{y}.parquet") for y in SEASONS}

def shots_of(df):
    return mx._add_preshot_context(df).filter(pl.col("event") == "shot")

shots = {y: shots_of(pbp[y]) for y in SEASONS}
all_shots = pl.concat(shots.values(), how="diagonal_relaxed")

def gt_show(g):
    display(HTML(g.as_raw_html()))
```

The PWHL coordinate expected-goals model estimates the probability that an
on-net shot becomes a goal, from pre-shot information only: shot geometry
(distance and angle to the net, derived from the HockeyTech rink coordinates),
shot type, rebound state, and the pre-shot movement context (what the previous
event was, how long ago, and how far away). It is a **logistic regression fit
at call time** in sdv-py (`sportsdataverse.pwhl.pwhl_xg_proxy.fit_pwhl_coord_xg`)
— there is no bundled artifact; the model is a deterministic function of the
play-by-play it is handed, which is what makes this document fully
reproducible from the data committed in this repository. A per-strength
(EV/PP/SH) Platt recalibration is applied on top of the base logit when the
frame carries strength columns. An alternative "shot-quality tier" proxy
exists for API stability but is not the production scorer; its two goal-named
tiers tautologically encode the outcome, a limitation the module documents
openly.

This document is the model's reproducible writeup: every number, figure and
table below is computed at render time from the committed play-by-play
parquet in `pwhl/pbp/parquet/`.

## Training data

```{python}
rows = []
for y in SEASONS:
    s = shots[y]
    rows.append({
        "season": y,
        "games": pbp[y]["game_id"].n_unique(),
        "pbp_events": pbp[y].height,
        "shots": s.height,
        "goals": int(s["goal"].cast(pl.Int64).sum()),
        "goal_rate": float(s["goal"].cast(pl.Float64).mean()),
        "coord_coverage": float(s["x_coord"].is_not_null().mean()),
    })
tbl = pl.DataFrame(rows)
gt_show(
    GT(tbl.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="PWHL committed play-by-play, by season",
                subtitle="on-net shots (event == 'shot'); computed at render time")
    .fmt_number(columns=["pbp_events", "shots"], sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_percent(columns=["goal_rate", "coord_coverage"], decimals=1)
)
```

The corpus is every season of PWHL play-by-play this repository has compiled
(the league launched in 2024), with shot coordinates at effectively full
coverage — the reason a coordinate xG is viable here at all. `strength_state`
exists league-wide because of the game-shifts backfill (T5/R4), and enters the
model through the `is_pp` / `is_sh` strength one-hots and the per-strength
recalibrator rather than as a raw feature.

## Exploratory data analysis

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Goal rate falls steeply with shot distance; the model's dominant feature."
geo = mx._shot_geometry(all_shots)
d = (
    geo
    .filter(pl.col("shot_distance").is_not_null())
    .with_columns((pl.col("shot_distance") / 5).floor().alias("bin"))
    .group_by("bin")
    .agg(pl.col("goal").cast(pl.Float64).mean().alias("goal_rate"),
         pl.len().alias("n"), pl.col("shot_distance").mean().alias("dist"))
    .filter(pl.col("n") >= 50)
    .sort("dist")
)
(
    ggplot(d.to_pandas(), aes("dist", "goal_rate"))
    + geom_point(aes(size="n"), color="#2a6f97", alpha=0.8)
    + geom_line(color="#2a6f97")
    + labs(x="shot distance (ft)", y="observed goal rate",
           title=f"Goal rate by shot distance — seasons {SEASONS[0]}–{SEASONS[-1]}")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Shot locations (offensive half, attacking to the right); goals in orange."
sm = (
    all_shots.select(
        pl.col("x_coord").abs().alias("x"), "y_coord",
        pl.col("goal").cast(pl.Int64).cast(pl.Utf8).alias("goal"))
    .drop_nulls()
    .sample(n=min(8000, all_shots.height), seed=7)
)
(
    ggplot(sm.to_pandas(), aes("x", "y_coord", color="goal"))
    + geom_point(alpha=0.25, size=0.7)
    + scale_color_manual(values={"0": "#9aa5b1", "1": "#e76f51"})
    + labs(x="|x| (ft from center; net at 89)", y="y (ft)",
           title="PWHL on-net shot map (all committed seasons)")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
st = (
    all_shots.group_by("strength_state")
    .agg(pl.len().alias("shots"), pl.col("goal").cast(pl.Float64).mean().alias("goal_rate"))
    .sort("shots", descending=True)
    .head(8)
)
gt_show(
    GT(st.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Shot mix and conversion by strength state")
    .fmt_number(columns="shots", sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_percent(columns="goal_rate", decimals=1)
)
```

The distance curve is the core of the model: conversion drops from over 20%
at the crease to low single digits beyond ~45 ft, and it is smooth enough that
a logistic in distance and angle captures most of the signal. The
strength-state table shows why strength enters the model: power-play shots
convert at a visibly higher rate than even-strength shots from a similar mix
of locations.

## Model, features & importance

```{python}
model_full = mx.fit_pwhl_coord_xg(pl.concat(pbp.values(), how="diagonal_relaxed"))
X_full, _, feat_frame = mx._build_xg_features(all_shots, want=model_full.features)
Xf = np.asarray(X_full, dtype=float)
sds = np.nanstd(Xf, axis=0)
coefs = np.asarray(model_full.model.coef_[0], dtype=float)
imp = pl.DataFrame({
    "feature": list(model_full.features),
    "coefficient": [float(c) for c in coefs],
    "std_importance": [abs(float(c)) * float(s) for c, s in zip(coefs, sds)],
}).sort("std_importance", descending=True)
gt_show(
    GT(imp.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Logistic coefficients and standardized importance",
                subtitle="importance = |coef| × sd(feature), full-corpus fit")
    .fmt_number(columns=["coefficient", "std_importance"], decimals=4)
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Standardized feature importance (|coef|·sd)."
impd = imp.filter(pl.col("std_importance") > 0).to_pandas()
(
    ggplot(impd, aes("reorder(feature, std_importance)", "std_importance"))
    + geom_col(fill="#2a6f97")
    + coord_flip()
    + labs(x="", y="|coef| × sd", title="PWHL xG feature importance")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

## SHAP-style attribution

For a linear-logit model the exact Shapley attribution of each feature on the
log-odds scale is `coef × (x − E[x])` — no approximation needed. The
distribution of per-shot attributions shows how each feature moves individual
shots, not just the average:

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Per-shot log-odds attributions (linear SHAP), top 8 features by importance; 2,000-shot sample."
mu = np.nanmean(Xf, axis=0)
contrib = (Xf - mu) * coefs
top = imp.head(8)["feature"].to_list()
idx = [list(model_full.features).index(f) for f in top]
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
samp = rng.choice(Xf.shape[0], size=min(2000, Xf.shape[0]), replace=False)
rows = []
for f, i in zip(top, idx):
    for s in samp:
        rows.append({"feature": f, "shap": float(contrib[s, i])})
shap_df = pl.DataFrame(rows).to_pandas()
(
    ggplot(shap_df, aes("feature", "shap"))
    + geom_jitter(width=0.25, alpha=0.08, size=0.5, color="#2a6f97")
    + coord_flip()
    + labs(x="", y="log-odds contribution  coef·(x−mean)",
           title="Linear SHAP attributions per shot")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

Distance dominates — its attributions span roughly ±1 log-odds — with rebound
state the strongest binary: a rebound shot gains about one log-odds (odds
×2.7) over a non-rebound shot from the same location.

## Evaluation

The honest test for a young league is a **season holdout**: fit on all
seasons before the newest, score the newest, and compare against a
constant-rate baseline.

```{python}
hold = SEASONS[-1]
train_pbp = pl.concat([pbp[y] for y in SEASONS[:-1]], how="diagonal_relaxed")
model_ho = mx.fit_pwhl_coord_xg(train_pbp)
sho = shots[hold]
xg_ho = model_ho.predict(sho).to_numpy()
y_ho = sho["goal"].cast(pl.Float64).to_numpy()
eps = 1e-9

def logloss(p, y):
    return float(np.mean(-(y * np.log(p + eps) + (1 - y) * np.log(1 - p + eps))))

def rank_auc(p, y):
    order = np.argsort(p)
    r = np.empty_like(order, dtype=float)
    r[order] = np.arange(1, len(p) + 1)
    n1 = y.sum()
    n0 = len(y) - n1
    return float((r[y == 1].sum() - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * n0))

base_rate = float(train_pbp.filter(pl.col("event") == "shot")["goal"].cast(pl.Float64).mean())
res = pl.DataFrame({
    "model": ["coordinate xG", "constant baseline (train goal rate)"],
    "logloss": [logloss(xg_ho, y_ho), logloss(np.full_like(xg_ho, base_rate), y_ho)],
    "rank_AUC": [rank_auc(xg_ho, y_ho), 0.5],
})
gt_show(
    GT(res.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title=f"Season-holdout evaluation — fit {SEASONS[0]}–{SEASONS[-2]}, scored on {hold}",
                subtitle=f"{sho.height:,} held-out shots, goal rate {y_ho.mean():.3f}")
    .fmt_number(columns=["logloss", "rank_AUC"], decimals=4)
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Holdout calibration by xG decile — points on the diagonal are perfectly calibrated."
dec = (
    pl.DataFrame({"xg": xg_ho, "goal": y_ho})
    .with_columns((pl.col("xg").rank("ordinal") * 10 / pl.len()).ceil().clip(1, 10).alias("decile"))
    .group_by("decile").agg(pl.col("xg").mean(), pl.col("goal").mean(), pl.len().alias("n"))
    .sort("decile")
)
(
    ggplot(dec.to_pandas(), aes("xg", "goal"))
    + geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0, linetype="dashed", color="gray")
    + geom_point(aes(size="n"), color="#2a6f97") + geom_line(color="#2a6f97")
    + labs(x="mean predicted xG (decile)", y="observed goal rate",
           title=f"Holdout calibration — {hold} season")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

The model beats the constant baseline on the held-out season and its decile
calibration tracks the diagonal. The published per-season assets on the
`pwhl_xg_pbp` release tag are scored by the same recipe with the full corpus
available at publish time; their in-sample evaluation lives in
[`pwhl_xg_eval_card.json`](pwhl_xg_eval_card.json).

## Per-season calibration

Three seasons now exist — enough to ask whether calibration holds season by
season as the league matures, not only on the newest one. Each season is
scored **leave-one-season-out**: the model is re-fit on the other seasons and
predicts the held-out one, so no season is scored by a model that saw it. The
per-season decile curves and the binomial calibration z-score
(`z = (goals − ΣxG) / sqrt(ΣxG · (1 − xG))`; a calibrated season has |z| ≲ 2
whatever its shot count) are computed at render time and extend automatically
as seasons land.

```{python}
loso = {}
for y in SEASONS:
    fit_pbp = pl.concat([pbp[s] for s in SEASONS if s != y], how="diagonal_relaxed")
    m = mx.fit_pwhl_coord_xg(fit_pbp)
    held = all_shots.filter(pl.col("game_season") == y)  # concatenated frame: strength columns present (null where unknown)
    loso[y] = (m.predict(held).to_numpy(), held["goal"].cast(pl.Float64).to_numpy())
rows = []
for y, (p, yy) in loso.items():
    xg_sum, var = float(p.sum()), float((p * (1 - p)).sum())
    rows.append({
        "season": y, "shots": len(yy), "goals": int(yy.sum()), "xG": xg_sum,
        "goals_per_xG": float(yy.sum()) / xg_sum, "z": (float(yy.sum()) - xg_sum) / np.sqrt(var),
        "logloss": logloss(p, yy), "rank_AUC": rank_auc(p, yy),
    })
season_cal = pl.DataFrame(rows)
gt_show(
    GT(season_cal.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Per-season calibration — leave-one-season-out",
                subtitle="each season scored by a model fit on the other committed seasons")
    .fmt_number(columns=["shots", "goals"], sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_number(columns=["xG"], decimals=1)
    .fmt_number(columns=["goals_per_xG", "z", "logloss", "rank_AUC"], decimals=3)
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Per-season calibration curves by xG decile (leave-one-season-out); the dashed line is perfect calibration."
dec_rows = []
for y, (p, yy) in loso.items():
    dec_rows.append(
        pl.DataFrame({"xg": p, "goal": yy})
        .with_columns((pl.col("xg").rank("ordinal") * 10 / pl.len()).ceil().clip(1, 10).alias("decile"))
        .group_by("decile").agg(pl.col("xg").mean(), pl.col("goal").mean(), pl.len().alias("n"))
        .with_columns(pl.lit(str(y)).alias("season"))
    )
dec_s = pl.concat(dec_rows).sort("season", "decile").to_pandas()
(
    ggplot(dec_s, aes("xg", "goal", color="season"))
    + geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0, linetype="dashed", color="gray")
    + geom_point(aes(size="n"), alpha=0.8) + geom_line()
    + labs(x="mean predicted xG (decile)", y="observed goal rate",
           title="Per-season calibration — leave-one-season-out")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

Read the table with the z column first: a season outside |z| ≈ 2 is one the
other seasons' shot-quality mix does not price correctly, and the decile curve
for that season shows *where* (crease vs perimeter) the miss sits. Two data
facts shape these rows. First, `strength_state` coverage differs sharply by
season (the 2024 and 2025 parquets carry no skater/strength columns at all,
2026 is ~99% covered — see the strength table above), so the `is_pp` / `is_sh`
features and the per-strength recalibrator are effectively active only for
2026 shots. Second, and a consequence of the first: the held-out rows here are
taken from the **concatenated** multi-season frame, not the single-season
parquet. Scored alone, a 2024 or 2025 frame lacks the strength columns and
`predict()` zero-fills the whole strength block *including* `is_home`, which
returns ~25% lower xG for the same rows (full-corpus in-sample mean xG 0.062
vs 0.082 goal rate) — a predict-path hazard for anyone scoring an early season
on its own.


## Results — players and teams

```{python}
xg_all = model_full.predict(all_shots)
scored = all_shots.with_columns(xg_all.alias("xg"))
latest = SEASONS[-1]
players = (
    scored.filter(pl.col("game_season") == pl.col("game_season").max())
    .group_by("player_id")
    .agg(
        pl.col("player_name_first").first(), pl.col("player_name_last").first(),
        pl.len().alias("shots"), pl.col("xg").sum().alias("xG"),
        pl.col("goal").cast(pl.Int64).sum().alias("goals"))
    .with_columns((pl.col("goals") - pl.col("xG")).alias("GAX"))
    .sort("xG", descending=True).head(15)
)
ros = pl.read_parquet(ROOT / "pwhl" / "rosters" / "parquet" / f"rosters_{latest}.parquet")
team_of = ros.group_by("player_id").agg(pl.col("team_abbr").last())
players = players.join(team_of, on="player_id", how="left").with_columns(
    ("<img src='https://assets.leaguestat.com/pwhl/240x240/"
     + pl.col("player_id").cast(pl.Utf8) + ".jpg' height='42'/>").alias("headshot"),
    (pl.col("player_name_first") + " " + pl.col("player_name_last")).alias("player"),
)
gt_out = (
    GT(players.select("headshot", "player", "team_abbr", "shots", "xG", "goals", "GAX").to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title=f"Top 15 skaters by expected goals — {latest} season",
                subtitle="xG summed over on-net shots; GAX = goals above expected")
    .fmt_markdown(columns="headshot")
    .fmt_number(columns=["xG", "GAX"], decimals=2)
    .cols_label(headshot="", player="Player", team_abbr="Team", shots="Shots",
                xG="xG", goals="G", GAX="GAX")
)
gt_show(gt_out)
```

```{python}
teams = (
    scored.filter(pl.col("game_season") == pl.col("game_season").max())
    .with_columns(pl.when(pl.col("team_id") == pl.col("home_team_id"))
                    .then(pl.col("home_team")).otherwise(pl.col("away_team")).alias("team"))
    .group_by("team")
    .agg(pl.col("game_id").n_unique().alias("games"),
         pl.col("xg").sum().alias("xG_for"),
         pl.col("goal").cast(pl.Int64).sum().alias("goals_for"))
    .with_columns((pl.col("xG_for") / pl.col("games")).alias("xG_per_game"))
    .sort("xG_per_game", descending=True)
)
gt_show(
    GT(teams.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title=f"Team shot generation — {latest} season")
    .fmt_number(columns=["xG_for", "xG_per_game"], decimals=2)
)
```

Positive GAX identifies finishers beating their shot quality; sustained
negative GAX at high xG identifies volume shooters running cold. Because the
league is three seasons old these player samples are small — GAX here is a
descriptive ledger, not a talent estimate.

## Provenance & reproducibility

- **Trained on:** every committed PWHL season in this repository
  (`pwhl/pbp/parquet/play_by_play_{2024..}.parquet`); the holdout evaluation
  fits on all seasons except the newest and scores the newest.
- **Model spec:** `sportsdataverse.pwhl.pwhl_xg_proxy.fit_pwhl_coord_xg`
  (logistic regression + per-strength Platt recalibration); no bundled
  artifact — deterministic re-fit from data.
- **Rebuild this document:** `scripts/render_model_docs.sh` (Quarto → GFM;
  uses this repo's `.venv` via `QUARTO_PYTHON`; deps in the `docs` group:
  `uv sync --group docs`).
- **Production surface:** stage `python/pwhl_model_01_xg_pbp.py` publishes
  xG-enriched per-season parquet to the `pwhl_xg_pbp` release tag
  (`pwhl_xg_cron.yml`); per-publish metadata in the card sidecars.
  Single home: `models/manifest.yaml`; registry row: `models/REGISTRY.md`.

## Avenues for improvement & open issues

- **EV/PP/SH-split models** — catalogued in `dev/t5_xg_reevaluation/`; the
  league-wide `strength_state` column exists precisely to enable this.
- **Resolved (2026-09-01, PR #PR_NUMBER_PLACEHOLDER):** *Per-season calibration
  drift* — the leave-one-season-out table and decile curves above recompute
  per-season calibration (goals/ΣxG, binomial z, AUC) at every render and
  extend automatically as seasons land.
- **Pre-shot passing data does not exist publicly** — royal-road one-timers
  are under-rated by construction; honest gains come from better rebound and
  rush definitions, not more features.
- **Known issue:** the published-release evaluation is in-sample; this
  document's season-holdout is the honest gate, and it should be re-run as
  each new season lands (the render does this automatically).
